Sequence/bundles below; backlog #8 was the **someday** vision row, retired by the owner 2026-10-28.

> **Reading this as a list rather than a document:** `python3 scripts/gen-backlog-page.py` renders
> every row below as a filterable page at **http://127.0.0.1:7391/backlog-table** (serve it with
> `python3 scripts/explainer-serve.py`). It opens with the open items grouped in plain English by
> *what they are* — which is the one thing this table cannot show, because severity ordering splits
> the six items that are all the same root cause. Counts there are derived from this file on every
> run, never from memory, and the grouping fails loudly rather than quietly omitting a new item.

## Items

> **Severity markers — read this before scanning for red.** A leading 🔴/🟠/🟡/🟢 records severity
> **at filing**. It is *not* a live state. **On close, replace the marker with ✅ and keep the
> original in parentheses** — `✅ (was 🔴)`. Measured 2026-08-17: #36 and #37 both still led with
> 🔴/🟠 while their own Status cells said **FIXED**, so anyone scanning markers — a person or a
> future session — would have counted a critical blocker that did not exist. The Status column is
> the truth; the marker is a headline, and a stale headline is worse than none.
>
> ⚠ **The Status column can only be the truth if the row HAS one.** Five rows once carried two of the

> paragraphs of literal `|` on GitHub. Both are now enforced by `check_backlog_table_shape` in

| 15 | 🟡 **Eager magazine-model generation at ingestion** — today the rendered "magazine model" (the Gemini editorial pass: prose → lead + labeled bullets, `generateMagazineModel`) is generated **lazily** on first owner HTML serve, which is why HTML isn't ready for every video and why #14 exists. The model is **cheap** — ~1–1.5¢ actual (6¢ reserved worst-case, `magazine_est_cents`), ~1/6 of the ~6.5¢ MD/summary cost (the summary pays for audio transcription; the model only reads the MD text). Making it eagerly at ingestion (~15–20% ingestion-cost bump) would make HTML **always ready** for the whole list — no 503, instant share/view — and delete the lazy-serve / reservation-lease machinery for the common path. | 20 | 🟠 **A title change orphans every dig blob — the slug half of the base is unguarded** — found 2026-08-04 during the `grill-with-docs` pass on the conditional-write spec, by asking what the phrase "the address moved" actually covers. A video's blob address is `base = pad(serialNumber) + '_' + slugify(title)`. **Nothing validates the slug half.** The worker derives it fresh from the job payload each run (`summary-handler.ts:96`, `slugify(payload.title)`); A3's `applySerial` (`lib/serial-filename.ts:20-25`) *preserves* whatever slug it finds and only re-prefixes the serial; and `checkSerialInvariant` (`lib/serial-invariant.ts:54`) only appears to check it — it builds its expectation with `applySerial(value, serial)`, copying the slug out of the value under test, so the slug comparison **cannot fail**. (A guard that passes in both worlds — the fourth instance on this project.) **Consequence, reachable with NO concurrency:** re-summarize a video whose YouTube title changed → same serial, new slug, so the row's `summaryMd` moves to `<serial>_<new-slug>.md` while every dig section blob stays at `dig/<serial>_<old-slug>/`. Today actor and owner are always the same principal, so this only clarifies which one wins when they diverge. **The payer is recorded on the GENERATION, not on a path** — a path can be re-pointed, copied into another user's view, or shadowed, and none of that should move a charge. Lands naturally on ADR-0007, which already treats artifacts as an append-only log of generations: payer becomes one more immutable field on the append. **② NON-DESTRUCTIVE SHARE.** The owner may add/update/delete their own artifacts. Everyone else may only *choose-if-multiple*, *add-their-own*, or *hide-from-their-own-view*. Nobody mutates anybody else's work. **This is enforceable as a DATABASE INVARIANT rather than application logic:** migration `0007`'s storage policy is `using (…split_part(name,'/',1) = auth.uid()) with check (…same…)`. **`with check` never changes** — you may only ever write under your own segment — and **only `using` widens** to workspace membership. So "others can add but never clobber" holds regardless of what any route does. **③ A PER-USER VIEW LAYER.** A view maps *(section → which generation I see)*, plus what the user has hidden or added. Rows, not blobs; cheap; and **the one thing that is never shared**. All per-user divergence lives here, which is what keeps the blob layer simple enough for ②'s one-clause change. "User-c sees both digs, or picks one" becomes a row update that never touches storage. **④ IMMUTABLE-IDENTITY ADDRESSING IS THE PREREQUISITE.** Many read paths may resolve to one blob; write uniqueness and read multiplicity stop conflicting once an address derives from immutable identity rather than display attributes. That is **exactly ADR-0006's thesis**, which the user re-derived independently from S3 semantics: *"Blob addresses are derived from immutable identity, not from display attributes."* Two digs of one section are two **generations**, each with its own address. **⚠ THE MEASURED BLOCKER (2026-08-18).** Today the dig key is `dig/<base>/<sectionId>.r<V>.md` — section and doc-version, **no author or generation dimension** — and **there is NO pointer/indirection layer**: `SupabaseBlobStore.objectKey()` feeds straight into `.upload()`, and a grep of `lib/storage/` for a manifest, blob-id or content-hash indirection returns **nothing**. So the path *is* the object, `dig-a` and `dig-b` write the same physical key, and the second **silently overwrites paid work**. The addressing violates the non-destructive policy before any code does — writing "non-destructive" into every route cannot help while the key has no room for two legitimate answers. Note `base = <serial>_<slug>` is derived from two *mutable* values, which is the same defect class as backlog #36: an address built from something that can change. **What the model DISSOLVES, recorded because these were live objections:** *revocation vs paid work* — hiding is a view operation, so no purchase is destroyed by someone else's preference; and *the concurrent double-dig race* — two users digging one section simultaneously is no longer a double charge but two legitimate artifacts, each paid by its own actor. That race was only a defect under the assumption of one dig per section. **⚠ ADR-0008 INTERACTION — needs re-derivation, not a tweak.** The serve money guard is corroboration-by-ordering and is valid only while one grant covers both objects. Widening `using` to a team breaks the *reasoning* quietly: reading the markdown would no longer prove anything about **this** user's access to the model, because they are different subjects. ADR-0008 exists precisely because that guard dies silently. **⚠ STILL GATED on unparking ADR-0006/0007 and the blob-addressing schema (user decision 2026-08-11, task #47) — but the case has changed:** that work was parked partly because its purpose was diffuse (correctness for its own sake). This direction gives it a product reason. **The two halves also separate:** *splitting* a playlist (membership + UI, no money, no parked ADR) can ship without *sharing* artifacts. **Prior art to read before any design work — do not start over.** ADR-0002 explicitly CONSIDERED and REJECTED video-level shared summaries, on **cost** not correctness; ADR-0006 supersedes that rejection in its own words (*"That objection no longer holds once the re-architecture is happening anyway"*) and names the mechanical price: drop `playlist_id` from `jobs_idem_active`, re-point the 1D spend FK, preserve the `(playlist_id, owner_id)` cross-tenant guard. ADR-0006 also already found that a uid-valued path segment grants its creator **unrevocable** access — so "the owner doesn't want to share" is not a separate issue today, it is structurally impossible to withdraw. Backlog #36 burned 13 rounds rediscovering a decision written down in three places; this entry exists to stop that recurring. | `docs/adr/0002`, `docs/adr/0006`, `docs/adr/0007`, `docs/adr/0008`, `jobs_idem_active`, spend FK, migration `0007` storage policy, dig addressing, a new per-user view table | L | (product / addressing) | **OPEN — filed 2026-08-18. NOT SCHEDULED and NOT being implemented; revisit when priority allows.** Design direction ①–④ recorded above from the 2026-08-18 discussion. Blocked on unparking blob addressing (task #47). |
